channel.title: Quality on Harness Engineer
channel.description: Recent content in Quality on Harness Engineer

item.title: Agent evals
item.description: OpenAI’s product guide for measuring agent quality with reproducible task-level and workflow-level evaluations.

item.title: AgentBoard
item.description: A benchmark for multi-turn LLM agents complemented by an analytical evaluation board for assessing model performance beyond final success rates, making partial-progress and trajectory quality visible.

item.title: AgentBoard: An Analytical Evaluation Board of Multi-turn LLM Agents
item.description: Introduces a fine-grained progress-rate metric and evaluation toolkit that makes partial-progress and trajectory quality visible, pushing agent evaluation beyond binary success rates.

item.title: An update on recent Claude Code quality reports
item.description: Postmortem of three separate changes that caused perceived Claude Code degradation — a reasoning-effort default change, a cache-optimization bug that dropped thinking history every turn, and a verbosity prompt that hurt coding quality — illustrating how harness changes slip past unit/e2e review and the eval/rollout practices needed to catch them.

item.title: AppWorld
item.description: A controllable world of apps and people for benchmarking interactive coding agents, with state-based and execution-based unit tests that surface harness quality around planning, code generation, and collateral-damage control.

item.title: Assessing internal quality while coding with an agent
item.description: Thoughtworks on moving quality checks into the loop instead of relying on after-the-fact manual review.

item.title: Galileo Agent Leaderboard
item.description: An open evaluation platform tracking LLM agents on task completion and tool calling across business domains, useful for comparing harness quality in enterprise-grade agentic scenarios.

item.title: Learning to Verify AI-Generated Code
item.description: OpenHands’ overview of a layered verification stack using trajectory critics trained on production traces for reranking, early stopping, and review-time quality control.

item.title: tau2-bench
item.description: A benchmark for realistic, multi-step agent tasks where success depends on tool use and execution quality rather than a single-shot answer.

item.title: The harness is all you need (mostly)
item.description: Practitioner argument that mastering one agent harness (Copilot) yields more than chasing tools/MCPs/models: a repeatable prototype → plan → autopilot → review → rubber-duck workflow that keeps context focused and uses sub-agents and cross-model review as quality gates.

item.title: The End of SWE-Bench Verified
item.description: OpenAI Frontier Evals leads Mia Glaese and Olivia Watkins explain why they publicly discontinued SWE-Bench Verified: >60% of remaining problems were unsolvable (overly narrow tests or hidden requirements), and contamination was demonstrable across all frontier models. Outlines the move to SWE-Bench Pro and the properties great coding evals need next: longer tasks, open-ended design decisions, code quality, real-world impact, and rubric-based human grading.
